 Rosemary’s Midtown
 Nestled in the heart of Manhattan's bustling Midtown East, Rosemary's Midtown brings the charm of our flagship West Village restaurant to one of NYC's most vibrant neighborhoods. Featuring housemade pastas, seasonal Italian dishes, and a curated spritz bar, our Midtown location offers a welcoming escape from the city's fast pace. Whether you're grabbing a quick lunch, unwinding after work, or enjoying a leisurely dinner, Rosemary's Midtown is your go-to destination for authentic Italian dining near Grand Central.

 Our Story
 Welcome to Rosemary’s, where our passion for seasonal Italian cooking and neighborly hospitality fuel our mission to bring people together. What is now a restaurant brand with three locations in New York, started back in the 1980s at my family’s kitchen table where every night my mom Rosemary poured her heart into cooking for me and my dad, Raul.
 While we moved around a lot when I was young — Europe, Asia, US — a few constants shone through: my father’s cherished copper pots that hung next to the kitchen table in every kitchen, and my mom’s devotion to her guests, expressed through her meticulous table settings and delicious cooking.
 Years later, when I began visiting my folks at their home in Lucca, with their gorgeous vegetable garden, or orto, and view from the dinner table overlooking the valley, I knew that I wanted to share their simple, elegant and heartfelt expression of hospitality with the world.
 Since opening Rosemary’s in the West Village in 2012, with its rooftop farm, string lights and view overlooking Jefferson Market Garden — all inspired by my folk’s home — the restaurant has grown into a neighborhood institution beloved by all walks of life.
 Over the years we’ve partnered with many incredible local groups, who share our values and passion for environmental stewardship and community engagement — from Brooklyn Grange, to PS41, to God’s Love We Deliver.
 If you appreciate quality seasonal cooking, everyday elegance and neighborly hospitality, I welcome you to come in for a meal and join the Rosemary’s community.
 Carlos Suarez
 Founder 
 Our Local Partners in Sustainability
 Beneath our dedication to service lies an unwavering commitment to forging a more sustainable future. Through numerous partnerships with local producers, in addition to our West Village rooftop garden, our fresh ingredients cater to diverse budgets without compromising quality or our values.
 At Rosemary’s, dining transcends the culinary experience — it is a celebration of thoughtful living rooted in cherished childhood memories. We extend a warm invitation for you to join a community that embraces hospitality, sustainability, and the joy of sharing exceptional pastas and wine — whatever the occasion may be.

 OUR STORY
 Nikkei is an intense intercultural exchange, expressing the diversity of flavors born from the union of the two age-old civilizations of Japan and Peru. It is an exciting cuisine whose identity is constantly being redefined and enriched. The name Sen Sakana – Japanese for “one thousand fish” – refers to the 1,000 different species that are said to swim in the waters off Peru.
 Opened initially as a non-kosher establishment in 2017, Sen Sakana quickly gained recognition as the best Nikkei restaurant in New York. When the pandemic forced Sen Sakana to close for most of 2020, restauranteur Allan Wartski saw this as an opportunity to reopen as a fully-certified glatt kosher restaurant. Since then, Sen Sakana has become an instant success with locals and tourists alike, serving delicious kosher Nikkei cuisine in an elegant setting.

 About
 In the 1850’s Japanese immigrants traveled to Peru to work on railroads, sugar plantations, and other agriculture jobs. They found a new home and gave Peru the rigor of their cuisine…orderly, intricate, and delicate. The Japanese and Peruvians shared the flavors and practices of their cultures, creating a new style of food: Nikkei Cuisine.
 Nikkei is an intense intercultural exchange, expressing the diversity of flavors born from the union of two age-old civilizations. It is a cuisine whose identity is constantly being redefined and enriched, making it an exciting one to work with. The name Sen Sakana – Japanese for “one thousand fish” – refers to the 1,000 different species that are said to swim in the waters off Peru.
 We invite you to taste our recipes, engage with our team, and explore the culinary romance of Japan and Peru.

 About
 a bit of history 
 F resh Salt is a neighborhood bar and café located at 146 Beekman Street, between Front and South, near the old Fulton Fish Market. The name comes from the faded advertisement on the front of the 1885 smokehouse we inhabit: Fresh, Salt, and Smoked Fish”.
 Since 2004, the bar has served as a refuge for an array of locals: from writers and start-ups on laptops, and office folks grabbing a tasty lunch by day,  to musicians, artists, locals and even the occasional sailor or two by night. We are proud to have been the last Seaport bar the Fulton Fish Market workers called home. With the area's recent revitalization, the bar now feels old-school, an homage to the neighborhoods history.
 Fresh Salt was nearly destroyed in the wake of Hurricane Sandy. Thanks to the amazing generosity and crowd sourcing of our friends, family and regulars, Fresh Salt was able to rebuild. The integrity and feel of the interior was maintained and even improved in some ways. Most people can't pick out what's different! We are proud to be a part of this close-knit community within the oldest neighborhood in New York. Fresh Salt is New York City's local.

 About Us
 Amity Hall is the premier sports destination of the Upper West Side best known for its lively atmosphere, handcrafted cocktails, and delicious food. Named after the once known Amity Street in the heart of Greenwich Village, Amity Hall was established in 2009 with the opening of its original location at 80 West 3rd Street. Its sister location opened at 982 Amsterdam Ave in 2015. Open seven days a week, Amity Hall features lunch, dinner and weekend brunch, and offers the perfect venue for hosting special events or watching a game. Official partner and supporter of Columbia Athletics.

 Madam Mikette's
 About us
 Madam Mikette’s brings together timeless recipes and a refined yet welcoming atmosphere in the heart of the city. Every dish is prepared with care, balancing classic inspiration with a modern touch. Whether you're joining us for a casual meal or a special evening, the experience is designed to feel both elevated and comfortable. It’s a space where good food and genuine hospitality come naturally. 
 Cocktails are our main focus with an extensive cocktail menu like no other in the neighborhood. Paying homage to the classic cocktail alongside seasonal and specialty cocktails we have something to tickle everyone's taste buds and keep you coming back for more.
 Our Name:
 On April 17, 1929, Mikette Cuba was fined $100.00 for the crime of illegal fortune telling. She made the fatal mistake of accepting 25 Cents from an undercover policewoman for a look into the future.
 From the late 1800's on, fortune telling tea rooms were all the rage among working class women throughout America. These Tea rooms flourished in big cities such as New York, and served as a major source of entertainment
 Our premises has been completely renovated to harken back to the vintage glamour of the 1920's.

 Our Story
 Savor the Bronx
 Nestled in the lobby of the historic landmark building the Clock Tower–formerly a piano factory–Charlies Bar & Kitchen remains at the forefront of a growing and evolving South Bronx. Every aspect of our historic home offers a unique blend of rustic sophistication and style, from the portraits of famous Charlies lining the walls, to our mixologist-crafted cocktail list. Our menus–lunch, brunch, and dinner–feature New American classics with Latin and Southern influences, using farm-fresh, sustainable ingredients from local purveyors. Coupled with a uniquely welcoming atmosphere among Bronx natives and newcomers alike, we seek to redefine what it means to dine in the South Bronx.
 Join us for a boozy Boogie Down Brunch every first Saturday of the month, or sample our cheese and charcuterie board for a candlelit date night. We welcome parties of 50 or more, and offer event packages for nearly any budget or level of service. In-house events have the option of hiring live bands, DJs, or even photobooths, while we offer a range of off-premise catering services that allow you to enjoy your favorite CBK offerings in the comfort of your own venue. We are firmly committed to providing the best experience possible for each patron who walks through our doors—let our service and culinary team customize a package and level of service that provides you with the ultimate experience. Again, thank you for considering Charlies Bar & Kitchen; we look forward to serving you.

 THE LEXINGTON SOCIAL is located in the up & coming SPANISH HARLEM, the heart of East Harlem, in 1634 Lexington Avenue. The Lexington Social is an intimate friendly neighborhood TAPAS WINE BAR offering specialty HAND-CRAFTED COCKTAILS & BEERS. 
 You are sure to enjoy the delicious Mediterranean style Tapas, extensive wine list, 8 tap beers (3 which of are seasonal), seasonal cocktails & SANGRIA all which will leave your taste buds wanting more.  About
 Celebrating 30 Years
 Arte Cafe on the Upper West Side is located in a landmark brownstone, steps away from Central Park and just west of beautiful Strawberry Fields. Celebrating over 30 years of service, this family-owned restaurant presents an upscale Italian cuisine with artisanal homemade pizzas and gourmet desserts. 
 At Arte Cafe, we take immense pride in crafting our signature dishes with the finest ingredients. We cook exclusively with Partanna Extra Virgin Olive Oil from Partanna, Sicily. Our chicken is Bell and Evans Free Range Organic Chicken, and our meats come from the world-renowned Pat LaFrieda. We import our Prosciutto directly from Italy and use Parmigiano that's aged for 24 months. Our San Marzano tomatoes hail from southern Italy, and our pastas are the premium DeCecco brand from Abruzzo for an unforgettable dining experience! These ingredients and many more are carefully selected by the owners and chefs. 
 Looking to celebrate a special occasion? Arte Cafe has private event rooms that cater to all budgets, perfect for both intimate gatherings and larger events. Come join us and make your next celebration truly memorable!
 Arte Cafe opened 30 years ago, however it all began when Dina Malta came to New York all the way from Italy in the 1960's. When her son, Robert, was a student in college, he opened his first restaurant in the early 1990's. With the help of his mother, he was able to run the location effectively. All of the original recipes, that are still used today, were created by her. "She had such a strong presence and always made sure the staff was cooking everything with the freshest, authentic ingredients", said her son, Robert. He recalled a time when one of the chefs in the kitchen wanted to use mozzarella on the dish, 'Chicken Parmigiana'. She said the dish is called 'Chicken Parmigiana' for a reason and you are supposed to use parmesan cheese. She always made sure every dish was made correctly and by hand. Although Dina has recently passed, her spirit lives on through Arte Cafe and the recipes today.

 Grub Food Menu 
 Conor's Goat is your friendly neighborhood Irish bar nestled on the lower eastside of New York City. Step into our cozy pub and experience the warmth of traditional Irish hospitality combined with the vibrant energy of the Big Apple. Indulge in our hearty pub fare, featuring classic comfort dishes crafted with love and care. From our savory Spinach & Artichoke Dip and crispy fish & chips to mouthwatering Goat'amole and Chips, our menu is a celebration of Irish-American culinary heritage. Pair your meal with a perfectly poured pint of Guinness or explore our selection of whiskeys and craft beers. Whether you're catching up with friends over a pint, enjoying the game, or simply seeking a taste of Ireland in the city that never sleeps, Conor's Goat is your go-to destination for good times and great food.

 11 TIGERS 
 New York City’s first-ever Speakeasy & Restaurant with a Thai heart & a Japanese soul.
 Our libations, crafted with the traditional Thai Yadong, including the signature 11 Tigers Yadong with a blend of 11 herbs, promise a unique journey for your taste buds.
 About us 
 Nestled in the heart of the East Village , 11 Tigers is New York City’s first speakeasy-inspired restaurant with Thai and Japanese influences that merges Japanese izakaya fare and Thai (sum yadongs) drinking cultures. The menu features such creations as Kee Mao Tiger Udon (a play on the Thai classic drunken noodles made with stir-fried Japanese noodles) and Black Panther Curry (squid ink fettuccine in makrut lime scented Thai Panang curry topped with ribeye steak). Ya Dong, the heart of cocktail culture at 11 Tigers, is a humble Thai medicinal liquor made in-house by infusing herbs over 3–5 days with rice spirits.
 Located on the second floor , the space is filled with sleek wood paneling adorned with Japanese-style tiger murals on each wall. Ample in size, you can share a booth with friends, snag a table with a date, or just sit at the bar.

 Fueled by passion, grit and a knack for artful innovation, David Burke is one of the best known and most respected chefs in modern American cuisine with his signature whimsical, boundlessly creative approach to food.  In addition to being an internationally celebrated chef, Burke is: a restaurateur; artist; philanthropist; businessperson; author; educator; art collector; puppeteer; minister; doctor of business administration, honoris causa; and beekeeper.  David Burke Hospitality Management (DBHM) owns, manages, licenses, and consults with restaurants, hotels, clubs, and schools worldwide. Currently, Burke and his DBHM team operate or orchestrate the culinary component of 18 restaurants, a historic event venue and a bakery. They also oversee a growing roster of David Burke branded products, including cookware, bakeware, steak sauce, cutlery, and wine. 
 Known for his industry insight, culinary accomplishments, business acumen and candid observations, Burke is often a leading contributor to major news sources, such as ABC TV, Forbes, Fox TV, Bloomberg and more. He is also frequently called upon to play the role of event honoree, speaker, and judge.
 In the parlance of today’s celebrity driven culture, he is a rock star of the culinary world. 
 Website: www.chefdavidburke.com 
 At just 26, Burke’s kitchen mastery won him the executive chef position of New York City’s legendary River Café, where he earned a prestigious three-star review from The New York Times . While at River Café, he became the first (and remains the only) American to win the prestigious Meilleurs Ouvriers de France Diplome d’Honneur, cementing his status as a leading chef on the global culinary stage. He subsequently won Japan’s Nippon Award for Excellence, and the Robert Mondavi Award of Excellence, all of which earned him a place in James Beard’s  Who’s Who of Food and Beverage in America.  Burke has been nominated twice for James Beard’s Best Chef and became a familiar face on the popular TV show “Top Chef.“
 After opening several restaurants with the founder of the iconic Smith & Wollensky steakhouse brand and, having established a remarkable reputation, Burke set his sights on growing his brand.  The first building block was the highly regarded David Burke & Donatella, which debuted in 2003. He went on to form a hospitality company that owned and operated numerous award-winning restaurants around the country.  It was during this period that Burke gained US patents for several innovations, including his famous Himalayan salt dry aging process for beef.
 In the early 1990s, Burke founded DB Global and later, in 2015, DBHM to further expand his footprint and to showcase what had become the culinary, decorative, and operational hallmarks of the David Burke brand.
 The early 2020 advent of the Covid-19 pandemic threatened that expansion; however, Burke continued to push forward.  He created the #Feed the Heroes program, which prepared and delivered more than 100,000 meals to frontline workers and charities.
 Sheer boredom during the months-long lockdown spurred his hugely popular and hilarious cooking demos “LeftobyDB,” with Lefto, a puppet bearing an uncanny resemblance to Burke with unruly gray hair, large-framed glasses, and chef’s coat. In addition, Burke launched a virtual online cooking demo program, CookinDB IGTV, and employee incentive initiatives tailor-made for Fortune 500 companies like Verizon.
 And, rather than retrenching, he opened eight new Burke-branded restaurants in North Carolina, Saudi Arabia, and his home state of New Jersey, where he now has seven restaurant operations and a bakery. Burke’s April 2022 purchase of 89-year-old Dixie Lee Bakery saved it from closure.
 In New Jersey, he also established the David Burke Scholarship at Brookdale Community College for which his annual donation of $10,000 pays the tuition for two students every year – one a culinary arts major, the other majoring in hospitality management.
 With the pandemic in the rear-view mirror, he is focusing on building a national presence for what is now Dixie Lee Bakery by David Burke and establishing Red Horse by David Burke as a burgeoning steakhouse brand.  To those ends, Dixie Lee’s products will soon be sold on Goldbelly and Amazon; South Lawn, NJ’s popular Fox & Falcon became Fox & Falcon by David Burke in Feb. 2023; and, a month later. The second Red Horse by David Burke debuted in White Plains, NY.
 In April 2023, Burke took on Cornelius, NC’ s Port City Club as his first lakeside establishment and the 18 th in his current restaurant portfolio.

 About RODNEY STRONG 
 Our story begins in 1959, when Rodney Strong envisioned Sonoma County as a special place for producing wine. A true pioneer in Sonoma County, Rodney Strong led the way for the future of Sonoma County winemaking. Rodney Strong Vineyards was the 13th winery bonded in the newly discovered Sonoma County wine industry.
 Today, led by the Klein family since 1989, Rodney Strong Vineyards is a family of passionate people committed to crafting premium wines, meaningful experiences and sustainable leadership in Sonoma County. We are united by our passion for wine and the belief that nothing brings people together better than sharing a great bottle of Rodney Strong wine.
 For over 30 years, RSWE has flourished under the leadership of the Klein Family, 4th generation California farmers. The Klein family is committed to protecting and preserving the environment in both the vineyards and at the winery through sustainable farming and winemaking.

 Pierre Loti Wine Bar is a beloved neighborhood wine bar located between Union Square and Gramercy Park, inspired by the charm and tradition of European wine culture. Our food selection is designed to complement our wines, with cheeses, small plates, and Mediterranean-inspired dishes crafted for pairing and sharing. 
 Whether you’re joining us for happy hour, dinner, or a late-night glass of wine, Pierre Loti offers a refined yet approachable experience filled with warmth, character, and true neighborhood charm.

 Burger Village is a popular restaurant located in park Slope at 222 7th Ave Brooklyn, NY 11215. The restaurant is known for its delicious and high-quality organic grass-fed burgers made with fresh, all-natural ingredients. Burger Village is committed to offering customers a healthier alternative to traditional fast food, with a menu featuring organic, grass-fed, antibiotic-free beef and plant-based and vegan burger options.
 In addition to our signature burgers, Burger Village also offers a variety of other menu items, including salads, sandwiches, fresh hand-cut French fries, and shakes. Customers can choose from a range of toppings and sauces to customize their meal to their liking or make it simple and delicious by picking up the signature pairs.
 Whether you’re in the mood for a classic burger or something a little more exotic, Burger Village has something for everyone. With its high-quality ingredients and commitment to sustainability, Burger Village has become a go-to destination for burger lovers in Park slope and beyond.

 Catering Services 
 Burger Village is a great spot for foodies who enjoy a good drink. In addition to the delicious and healthy food options, the restaurant offers a wide variety of signature cocktails, fine draft beers, local beers, and organic wines to complement your meal.
 The signature cocktails at Burger Village are made using only the freshest ingredients and are carefully crafted to offer a unique and flavorful experience. You can choose from a range of options, including classic cocktails, like the Manhattan or Old Fashioned, or try one of their original creations, like the Spicy Mango Margarita or the Cucumber Cooler.
 For beer enthusiasts, Burger Village offers a selection of fine draft beers and local beers from some of the best local breweries. Beer is available for every taste preference, from pale ales to Ipa’s.

 Fresh from the Farm, Straight to Your Plate
 Burger Village is the brainchild of four Long Island brothers – “Sam, Nick, Vick, and Ravi”! They
 bring over two decades of experience in the food service and restaurant management industries.
 With backgrounds in operating both quick-service restaurants (QSRs) and full-service
 restaurants, each brother brings a unique strength to Burger Village, creating a comprehensive
 and high-quality dining and catering experience.
 Founded in 2013 in Great Neck, NY, Burger Village was born out of a shared passion for organic
 food and healthy lifestyles. Our mission is simple – to provide fresh, organic meals with
 exceptional service.
 We’ve grown since then, with locations across New York including Tribeca, Farmingdale, Huntington Station, Tanger Outlet Deer Park, Hicksville, Brooklyn, White Plains and Fresh Meadows. We've also made our mark in California.

Burger Village

 to bison, elk, and wild boar, our meats are rich in flavor and nutrition. We also cater to

 Welcome To Saperavi 
 Authentic Georgian Dining in NYC
 Explore Saperavi, an authentic Georgian restaurant, for a delicious experience. Our fresh and delightful dishes bring the comforting vibes of our country, Georgia, to your table. Join us for a simple yet delicious culinary journey in our authentic eateries, featuring both indoor and outdoor seating.   
 At Saperavi, you can transport yourself to the heart of Georgia's wine culture without leaving NYC! Our bistro is located at 14th St. at 2nd Ave. Our restaurants uptown East & West are at 2nd Ave. at E. 89th St. and at 410 Amsterdam Ave. at W. 80th. 
 Book a Table 
 Since 1990
 Georgian Wine
 The name “Saperavi” is derived from a celebrated Georgian wine, crafted from the distinctive Saperavi grape, renowned for its deep, robust flavors. 
 Enjoy our outdoor patio and savor our extensive wine list.  
 Georgia is recognized as the birthplace of winemaking, with evidence dating back over 8,000 years. We are dedicated to sharing this legacy with you, pairing exquisite Georgian wines with our authentic cuisine.

 Authentic Georgian Hospitality on 14th Street
 Tucked into one of Manhattan’s most vibrant dining corridors, Saperavi’s East Village restaurant is a warm, conversational room built around Georgia’s centuries-old hospitality tradition—the Supra (feast). Our space beautifully accommodates solo diners searching for a glass of amber wine at the bar, romantic patio dates, and long, lingering tables for group get-togethers. Our kitchen runs on a single principle: every dish should taste as if it came straight from a home kitchen in Tbilisi.
 Our 14th Street corridor pulls in a beautifully diverse crowd—NYU students, local Stuyvesant Town residents, post-work groups walking up from Union Square, and international wine enthusiasts hunting for the city’s deepest qvevri-method wine selection. Come tear into a fresh, clay-oven baked Adjarian Khachapuri cheese boat, enjoy hand-twisted Khinkali dumplings, or share a colorful spread of vegetable Pkhali . We highly recommend securing table reservations for weekend dinner service.

 East Village Bistro FAQs
 Do you offer outdoor seating at the East Village branch?
 Yes, our East Village bistro features a charming outdoor dining patio on 14th Street that accommodates up to 10 guests, alongside an intimate 20-seat indoor dining layout. Patio seating is subject to daily weather conditions and availability.
 Which subway lines drop off closest to the restaurant?
 We are exceptionally accessible; the 1st Ave L train station sits just moments away, while the major 14th St-Union Square station (servicing the 4, 5, 6, L, N, Q, R, W lines) is less than a five-minute walk from our front door. 
 I have never tried Georgian food. What should I order first?
 Start with a khachapuri, a plate of khinkali and something from the cold table — that trio covers the three things Georgian cooking is best known for. Our Adjaruli khachapuri arrives as a boat of molten Georgian cheese topped with butter and an egg yolk you stir in at the table. Khinkali are hand-pleated dumplings filled with seasoned meat, spinach and cheese, or mushrooms. Add Assorted Pkhali — vegetable and walnut rolls served with house cornbread — and you have a proper introduction to the table.
 Do you have vegetarian and vegan options in the East Village?
 Yes — Georgian cooking is unusually generous to plant-based eaters, and a large share of our menu contains no meat at all. Ajapsandali (eggplant, tomato and bell pepper), Assorted Pkhali , Lobio bean stew, Lobiani bean bread, the house pickles and our grilled and roasted vegetables are all meat-free. Vegetarians who eat dairy can also order Spinach and Cheese or Mushroom Khinkali and any of our cheese khachapuri . Let your server know you are eating vegan and they will point you to the dishes made without dairy.
 Do you offer takeout and delivery in the East Village?
 Yes. You can order Georgian food for pickup or delivery from our 14th Street kitchen through our online ordering page . The clay-pot stews, khinkali and lobiani all travel well. We do recommend eating khachapuri soon after pickup, while the cheese is still molten.
 What time do you open, and when is happy hour?
 Our East Village bistro is open daily from 10:00 AM to 11:00 PM, and happy hour runs Monday through Friday from 2:00 PM to 6:00 PM. The 10:00 AM opening makes us one of the earlier sit-down options on 14th Street, and the late close suits dinner after a show or an evening walk around Union Square. For the patio or a larger table, we recommend booking ahead .

 Authentic Georgian Cuisine in the Heart of the UWS
 Saperavi NYC proudly brings the comforting, ancient culinary flavors of Georgia straight to Manhattan's Upper West Side. Nestled on vibrant Amsterdam Avenue, our restaurant features a spacious and warm full-service dining atmosphere, making it a beloved gathering spot for locals, neighborhood families, and theater-goers alike.
 If you are planning an unforgettable dinner before a performance at nearby Lincoln Center, winding down after a day of discovery at the American Museum of Natural History, or exploring Central Park, Saperavi UWS offers the perfect culinary destination. Our traditional kitchen fires up the clay oven daily to bake golden, molten Adjarian Khachapuri cheese boats right to your table, alongside steaming platters of handmade spiced Khinkali dumplings. Pair your meal with an exceptional selection of authentic qvevri amber (orange) or bold red wines to complete the ultimate Georgian dining experience.
 Why Saperavi is the Go-To Georgian Restaurant on the Upper West Side
 The Upper West Side (UWS) is celebrated for its cultural landmarks, scenic parks, and diverse dining scene. At Saperavi NYC, we add a completely unique flavor profile to this historic neighborhood. Georgian cuisine is a masterclass in culinary balance—blending fresh herbs, rich walnuts, garlic, and unique spices like blue fenugreek and marigold.
 Our menu is built on family recipes passed down through generations, utilizing authentic ingredients sourced directly from Georgia to ensure that every bite of Khachapuri or sip of Qvevri wine is completely authentic.
 A Warm, Cozy Ambiance in the Heart of Manhattan
 We designed our Upper West Side location to feel like a traditional Georgian home ( oda ). With rustic accents, warm lighting, and a welcoming atmosphere, Saperavi NYC is perfect for:
 Intimate Date Nights: Share a bubbling skillet of cheese and a bottle of ancient amber wine.
 Family Gatherings: Georgian dining is inherently communal, designed for sharing large plates and passing dishes around the table.
 Casual Weekday Dinners: Treat yourself to a comforting bowl of Georgian soup or stew after a long day of exploring the city.
 Our Signature UWS Menu Highlights
 If you've never experienced Georgian food before, your palate is in for an extraordinary treat. If you're already a lover of the cuisine, our authentic execution will feel like home.
 1. Khachapuri (Georgian Cheese Bread)
 No Georgian meal is complete without Khachapuri . We serve several variations of this iconic dish, baked fresh to order in our stone ovens:
 Adjaruli Khachapuri: The famous boat-shaped bread filled with a molten blend of Sulguni cheese, topped with a raw egg yolk and a pat of butter. Mix it at the table and dip the crust!
 Imeruli Khachapuri: A circular, double-layered flatbread stuffed to the brim with warm, gooey Georgian cheese.
 2. Khinkali (Giant Soup Dumplings)
 Our Khinkali are hand-rolled and stuffed with seasoned minced meat (beef and pork blend) or wild mushrooms, spiked with fresh herbs and broth.
 How to eat them: Grab the dumpling by its thick doughy handle (the “crown”), turn it upside down, take a small bite to suck out the delicious, savory broth, and then eat the rest—leaving the crown on your plate!
 3. Saperavi's Signature Mains
 Chashushuli: A fragrant, slow-simmered beef stew cooked with fresh tomatoes, garlic, bell peppers, and a robust blend of Georgian spices.
 Shkmeruli: Juicy roasted chicken swimming in an intensely aromatic garlic and milk/cream sauce, served sizzling in a clay pot.
 Experience 8,000 Years of Winemaking History
 Georgia is widely recognized as the birthplace of wine, boasting an unbroken 8,000-year history of viticulture. At Saperavi NYC, we honor this legacy with a curated list of natural Georgian wines , many of which are fermented in Qvevri —large clay vessels buried underground.
 We offer an exceptional selection of red, white, and skin-contact “amber” (orange) wines , including:
 Saperavi : A deep, dry, inky red wine with notes of dark berries and wild spices.
 Rkatsiteli: A crisp, structurally complex white wine fermented on its skins to create a beautiful amber hue.
 Our knowledgeable staff is always happy to recommend the perfect wine pairing to complement your meal.

 Do you offer pre-theater dining for Lincoln Center attendees?
 Yes, our full-service dining room on Amsterdam Avenue opens daily at 11:00 AM, making it an excellent destination for quick lunch options, pre-theater dinners, or late-night drinks and dessert after a show. We recommend securing your table reservation on OpenTable to keep perfectly on schedule with your performance curtains.
 What is the easiest transit path to Saperavi UWS?
 Our Upper West Side restaurant is highly accessible via public transit. We are located just a 3-minute walk from the 79th St Subway station (1 local train) and less than 10 minutes from the 81st St-Museum of Natural History station (B and C lines). The M7 and M11 local buses drop off conveniently along Amsterdam Ave steps away from our doors.
 Do you offer vegetarian and vegan options?
 Yes! Georgian cuisine is incredibly friendly to vegetarians and vegans. Many of our cold appetizers (like Pkhali walnut spreads ) are naturally vegan, and we offer vegetarian versions of Khachapuri, Khinkali, and clay-pot stews.
 Can I make a reservation for a large group?
 Absolutely. Georgian dining is meant to be enjoyed in large groups. We recommend making reservations online via our website for parties of 6 or more to ensure we can accommodate you comfortably.
 Do you offer delivery and takeout on the UWS?
 Yes, you can order your favorite Georgian comfort food for pickup or delivery directly through our website or our delivery partners.

 Authentic Georgian Dining on the Upper East Side
 Saperavi NYC brings the unmatched culinary traditions of the country of Georgia right to the heart of Yorkville and the Upper East Side. Unlike our intimate companion bistro in the East Village, our 2nd Ave restaurant boasts an expansive, full-size dining room layout designed to accommodate celebratory neighborhood gatherings, family feasts, and romantic date nights alike.
 Whether you are planning a post-museum lunch after touring the nearby Metropolitan Museum of Art and Guggenheim along Museum Mile, or wrapping up an afternoon stroll through Central Park, our kitchen provides a warm, welcoming sanctuary. We feature a state-of-the-art clay oven baking hot, pulling cheese-filled Adjarian Khachapuri fresh to order, alongside traditional main courses perfectly suited to pair with our historic, skin-contact orange and bold red Georgian wines.

 Upper East Side Dining FAQs
 Can you accommodate large group parties or private dining?
 Yes, our Upper East Side location features an expansive, multi-room dining configuration uniquely optimized for hosting large corporate events, private family parties, and traditional multi-course Georgian Supra feasts. Please utilize our Catering & Events Form to lock in your custom group reservations.
 How close is Saperavi UES to NYC transit links?
 Saperavi Upper East Side is highly accessible via public transit, located just a 3-minute walk from the 86th St Subways station servicing the Q train, as well as the 4, 5, and 6 express/local lines. Additionally, the M86-SBS cross-town bus drops off steps away from our front entrance on 2nd Ave.
 What is Georgian cuisine, and how is it different from Russian or Mediterranean food?
 Georgian food comes from the country of Georgia in the Caucasus, and its signature is the combination of walnut, garlic, fresh herbs and spices such as blue fenugreek and marigold. Unlike Russian cooking, it leans heavily on ground-walnut sauces and sour-fruit seasoning; unlike Mediterranean cooking, it is built around clay-oven cheese breads, filled dumplings and slow-simmered clay-pot stews. Georgia is also the world's oldest wine culture, with roughly 8,000 years of continuous winemaking .
 Do you have vegetarian and vegan dishes on the Upper East Side?
 Yes, and more than most guests expect — a large share of the Georgian table is naturally meat-free. Ajapsandali (eggplant, tomato and bell pepper), Assorted Pkhali , Lobio bean stew, Rustic Eggplant Salad, our house-pickled vegetables and the chargrilled seasonal vegetables all come without meat. Vegetarians who eat dairy should look at Pkhlovana, the spinach-and-cheese khachapuri , or the Potato Mushroom Ojakhuri. Tell your server you are eating vegan and they will point you to the plates made without dairy.
 Do you serve Georgian wine, and can the staff recommend a pairing?
 Yes — our list is built around Georgian bottles, including the deep red Saperavi our restaurant is named for and skin-contact amber whites such as Rkatsiteli. Many are fermented in qvevri , the buried clay vessels Georgians have used for thousands of years. Ask your server for a pairing — our team is used to walking guests through amber wine for the first time.
 Is Saperavi a good stop before or after visiting Museum Mile?
 Yes. We are on 2nd Avenue at 89th Street, a short walk east of the Museum Mile stretch of Fifth Avenue and Central Park, and we are open daily from 11:00 AM to 11:00 PM. That covers a late lunch between galleries as well as a full dinner afterward, and happy hour runs Monday through Friday from 2:00 PM to 6:00 PM.

 About Us
 Experienced Professionals 
 Mission
 Provide the opportunity for our guests to experience the culture, and the unique and vibrant flavors of Georgian wine and cuisine 
 Values
 Excellence in every dish and glass of wine, honoring the storied traditions and quality that define Georgian gastronomy. 
 Venue 
 A small, intimate bistro on 14th Street (East Village at 2nd Ave) and two full-size restaurants on the Upper East and West sides of NYC. 
 Our Concept
 Vision
 Saperavi NYC is an authentic Georgian restaurant and wine bar chain with three locations across Manhattan: the East Village, Upper East Side, and Upper West Side. Named after Georgia’s legendary native dark-skinned grape, we honor an 8,000-year culinary and winemaking legacy, bringing the warm hospitality of the traditional Georgian Supra feast to New York City.
 ABOUT GEORGIAN WINE
 Nestled at the crossroads of Europe and Asia, Georgia is a treasure trove for wine enthusiasts, boasting an unparalleled viticultural heritage that dates back over 8,000 years—making it one of the oldest wine-producing regions in the world.
 Georgian wine is not just a beverage; it's a vibrant tapestry woven with history, culture, and tradition. The country’s unique fermentation method in qvevri—large clay vessels buried underground—infuses these wines with distinctive flavors and character you cannot find elsewhere.
 With over 500 indigenous grape varieties flourishing in this fertile soil, every bottle offers a glimpse into Georgia's diverse terroir—from crisp whites to bold reds—the spectrum is nothing short of breathtaking!
 We're excited to introduce you to Georgian wine. It embodies not merely taste but also our history and culture. Share it with us.

 Questions, answered
 Where is The Drunken Munkey located? 
 + 
 The Drunken Munkey is at 338 East 92nd Street, between First and Second Avenues on Manhattan's Upper East Side, New York, NY 10128.
 What are your hours? 
 + 
 We're open Monday to Thursday 4:00 pm–12:00 am, Friday 4:00 pm–1:00 am, Saturday 11:00 am–1:00 am, and Sunday 11:00 am–12:00 am. The kitchen closes one hour before we close.
 Do you serve weekend brunch? 
 + 
 Yes — weekend brunch is served Saturday and Sunday, 11:00 am–3:30 pm. Standout dishes include the Biryani Breakfast Bowl , the Splendid Short Ribs Benedict , and the Bombay Berry French Toast .
 Is there a Happy Hour? 
 + 
 Yes — Happy Hour runs every day, 4:00–6:00 pm, with five select cocktails.
 Do you take reservations? 
 + 
 Yes. You can reserve a table online , and for parties of nine or more, email KingKong@drunkenmunkey.com .
 Do you offer delivery or takeout? 
 + 
 Yes — order delivery and takeout through Uber Eats .
 Do you have vegetarian options? 
 + 
 Plenty. Vegetarian dishes are marked (v) on the menu, and (n) flags nuts. An allergy menu is available on request.
 What is the Munkey Meal? 
 + 
 Every night from 10 pm we serve a hot meal to anyone in need — vegetarian or non-vegetarian. Just ask the host. Guests can pay it forward by sponsoring a meal for $7 .

 Our Story 
 A little Old Bombay on 92nd Street 
 family recipes, four generations on
 Est. 
 2013 
 Two friends, one table
 The Drunken Munkey began with two childhood friends. Arun Mirchandani and Chirag Chaman grew up in Army families, where some of the best meals were the ones served in the mess hall — generous, unfussy, made to feed everyone at the table.
 Arun came to it trained: a graduate of the Welcomgroup Graduate School of Hotel Administration in Manipal, the hotel school that produced Michelin-starred chef Vikas Khanna, then years in restaurants, bars and hotels. He had lived on the Upper East Side since 2003 and wanted a cocktail bar of his own up here. He opened The Drunken Munkey on East 92nd Street in 2013, the first room in the neighborhood to make the cocktail the point rather than a short list printed beside the food.
 Underneath the bistro is a tribute to the Irani cafés of old Bombay: Leopold, Britannia, Yazdani, Empire. It is the neighborhood spot Arun had always wanted, in his own backyard.
 From the family kitchen 
 Recipes carried across a partition , kept across generations.
 Ask which version of an Indian dish is the correct one and there is no answer worth having. These recipes grew up in houses, one kitchen at a time, each with its own hand on the spices, so the same chicken curry can taste different two doors apart and neither cook is wrong. What is left is heritage: family recipes, kept and handed on.
 Most of them came from Arun's grandmother, Savitri Mirchandani, who was Dadima at home. She left Karachi by ship in 1947 with a suitcase, two small children and a heavy brass hamam dasta that one of her maids had hidden in the luggage. Mum's Lemon Daal is her recipe folded together with Arun's mother's. The First-Class Railway Chicken is her chicken curry. The chilli cheese toast he learned from her. She was here on the first night in 2013 with her prayer book, she turned a hundred in this room in September 2022, and she died in March 2026, at 103.
 The long version of her story runs in the Munkey Times: The Recipes My Grandmother Carried .
 Many of the vegetarian dishes come from Arun's mother, Vasanti, who is South Indian and picked up a great many of Dadima's recipes herself. She lives close by and still spot-checks the kitchen, thirteen years in. This is home-style cooking, served in a proper bistro setting.
 “It really comes down to heritage. Family recipes, passed down through generations. From my great-grandmother to my grandmother to my mother, now to me.”
 Arun Mirchandani · Founder
 Behind the bar
 The cocktail, tracing home
 Arun is the soul of the Munkey — a collector of the craft, from vintage bar tools to the stories behind a drink. He built the bar around a simple idea: that the cocktail itself traces back to India.
 Punch turns up in English in 1632, in a letter written from India, and it turns up with five parts: alcohol, sugar, lemon, water, spice. Paanch is Hindi for five. The bowl had been going round the table for the better part of two centuries before English produced the word cocktail.
 The House Paanch has been on the list since the first night. Lupe Toxtli, who runs the bar, builds it on a spiced syrup made here, with fresh fruit and a combination of spirits and liqueurs he has no intention of writing down. It comes by the glass, or by the bowl for a table that wants to share one.

 Everyone eats
 That mess-hall spirit runs through everything, right down to the Munkey Meal — a hot meal served nightly to anyone in need, which our guests keep going by sponsoring a plate for just $7.

 A word about 
 Ghee
 We cook some dishes in ghee, and we make it fresh in-house. Butter is reduced over a low flame for hours until the milk solids caramelize and separate out, which leaves a fat with a very high smoke point and a sweet, nutty flavor.
 Because that process takes the dairy out of the finished product, ghee keeps far longer than butter and sits well with a lot of people who are lactose intolerant. It is not, however, dairy-free — so if dairy is a true allergy for you rather than an intolerance, tell your server and the kitchen will cook around it.

 About 
 Sugar Bar was established in 1996 by Nickolas Ashford one half of the songwriting and performing sensation Ashford Simpson. Co-owned with his wife Valerie Simpson, Sugar Bar offers an intimate and elegant ambiance offset by African artifacts to give you the feel of hidden village on the trendy upper West side of Manhattan. 
 Sugar Bar is best known for its sensational cuisine and live entertainment. Since its inception, the Sugar Bar has been a hotspot for so many celebrities such as Stevie Wonder, Berry Gordy,BeBe Winans, Freddie Jackson, Whoopi Goldberg, Michael Douglas, Stephanie Mills, Brandy, Alicia Keys, Cyndi Lauper, Jessie J and legends Dr. Maya Angelou, Quincy Jones & Andre Leon Talley to name a few. 
 If you haven't heard about Sugar Bar's Open Mic Thursdays you don't know what you're missing. It is truly a night of pure entertainment and folks from all around the world are tuning in virtually. Check us out on alternative nights as well showcasing local and international talent from R&B, Soul, Jazz, Gospel to Caribbean and Traditional African Rhythms. 
 Come enjoy some of our signature cocktails like the “Street Corner” named after the owners own musical hit or the classic Sugartini. And don't miss out on some of the menu favorites like New Zealand Lamb Chops or Crispy Fried Chicken. Whether you dine in our main dining room with an excellent view of the stage or the more intimate setting of our enclosed garden room in the back with big screen access to shows, you will feel at home and see why everyone keeps coming back. With the new addition of our outdoor dining, you can also enjoy our new Brunch menu w/ the summer breeze.

 Welcome to Nurse Bettie
 Opened in 2006, Nurse Bettie has become an institution on the Lower East Side of Manhattan. Inspired by the pin-up art and culture of the 1950's, cocktails are crafted with a nod to the classics and a twist on the contemporaries. As an intimate space with a casual setting, nights can be met with either a DJ to keep the night going late or one of the longest running burlesque shows in New York City. Focused on hospitality, we are committed to providing excellent cocktails in an inviting and exciting atmosphere. With 18 years of experience, we look forward to seeing you soon!

 about us
 Hailed by Grub Street as,”… a glowing fairy-tale jewel box filled with delights ,” LunÁtico was founded in 2014 by musicians Richard Julian , Arthur Kell, & Rosita Késs. Having performed themselves in bars and venues across the globe, as well as sharing a passion for food, wine, and spirits, the trio routinely kicked around the idea of opening their own. Their idea was to combine the sophisticated elements of the cocktail bars they loved with the funkiness of their favorite music spots. 
 A “sign” they should follow through on their ambitions came one afternoon when Arthur happened to drive past Larry’s Liquid Love (A Sophisticated Meeting Place) in his Plymouth Voyager as they were removing their sprawling banner and putting it out with the trash. The three had long shared a bemusement for the iconic neighborhood fixture and now it was in their possession! How could they not imagine it on the wall of their own future establishment? 
 Many sweet triumphs, hard lessons, nights of transcendent music, and a global pandemic later, the remaining owners, Arthur Kell and Richard Julian , continue to combine a first-rate cocktail menu with delicious food and one of the most diverse music programs in New York City and beyond. We hope you enjoy it as much as we do.
 Richard Julian 
(co-owner)
 Lured into the bar business by his passion for tequila, co-founder Richard Julian is better-known as a widely-acclaimed songwriter and recording artist. Having released six albums (including 2006's critically-acclaimed Slow New York) he has toured the globe as a solo artist as well as with The Little Willies, a side-project featuring Norah Jones.
Richard cherishes the opportunity LunÀtico provides - to champion the music and musicians he loves.
 Arthur Kell
(co-owner)
 Having started out his musical life playing in Bed-Stuy bars in the 80s, perhaps it was only a matter of time before co-founder Arthur Kell returned to open his own. But when he's not busy tending to the needs of the LunÀtico bands and patrons, Arthur enjoys a career as an acclaimed bassist and composer. His group regularly tours Europe including the Copenhagen and Madrid jazz festivals. His extensive travels in Africa left a profound mark on his own compositions and helped to shape the diverse roster of talent at Bar LunÀtico.
 Outside of music, Arthur is an avid activist with a passion for environmental issues. He coordinated that work for NYPIRG for ten years stopping the proposed Brooklyn Navy Yard incinerator.

 Sala Astoria- 
 Authentic Spanish Tapas in Astoria, NY 
 Step into the vibrant world of Sala Astoria in the heart of Astoria, Queens! Since our beginning on the Bowery in 1999, our mission has been to transport you to an authentic Spanish experience. By authentic, we mean offering you a warm, inviting experience that lovingly pays tribute to the rich history of genuine Spanish cuisine. 
 We offer a menu full of classic tapas, paella, and fine wines served in a casual, elegant space. Whether you're joining us for dinner, a special celebration, or a private event, Sala Astoria brings the spirit of Spain to New York in every plate and every gathering. 
 Come visit us! 
 PINCHOS, TAPAS, PAELLA AND MORE 
 At Sala, we devote the "tapas" section of our menu to the vast world of pinchos. However, the core of our culinary offerings unfolds in the numerous choices within our "raciones" section—delightful dishes crafted for sharing among small or large groups. In addition to our pinchos and raciones, our menu is further enriched by hearty Platos, authentic Paella, Arroces, and a sweet finale with our inviting Postres. Explore the true Spanish flavors that cater to every palate.

 OUR STORY 
 Sagaponack has been open for over a decade. It was named after the first owner's favorite town in the Hamptons. In October 2020, our team was brought in to bring new energy and flare to the restaurant. 
We offer a unique take on your beachfront seafood classics, with menu options like oysters, lobster rolls, and a surf & turf burger. 
 WE PUT
QUALITY FIRST
 Our menu is thoughtfully crafted using ingredients sourced from local, reputable vendors who share our commitment to excellence. A true standout on our menu is the Peeko oysters, harvested from the pristine waters of Long Island. Their fresh, briny flavor embodies the very essence of coastal elegance. At SAGA, every dish tells a story of tradition, innovation, and passion. Join us and discover the difference of dining with care, creativity, and community at our core.

 The Jewel of the Upper East Side
 A culinary cornerstone of Manhattan, Cafe D'Alsace has been a neighborhood favorite for nearly two decades. Awarded two stars by the New York Times, we offer Alsatian cuisine in a familiar, yet uniquely special setting, blending German and French culinary influences and service traditions. 
 Our Story 
 Tradition & Excellence
 So named for the Alsace region of northeastern France, our diverse menu features classic Alsatian favorites, alongside ever-changing seasonal specials. Think Tarte Flambée, Choucroute Garnie and our exceptional house-made desserts, plus a beverage program that includes over 130 beers, and a dedicated in-house cicerone.

 Our Story
 An Upper East Side Institution
 From our elegantly curved zinc bar, adorned with antique seltzer bottles, to the vibrant hues of our terrazzo floors, every corner of our restaurant radiates cozy charm.
 For 15 years, we proudly served our community from the southwest corner of 88th Street and 2nd Avenue before relocating just a block away to a historic site—the former home of Elaine's, a beloved neighborhood institution for over 50 years. Today, we continue our legacy of warm, dedicated service. Many of our regulars consider Café D'Alsace an extension of their own kitchens, a testament to our deep connection with our community.
 Proudly New York-owned and operated, we prioritize sourcing locally whenever possible, embracing our role in this vibrant city, resulting in our two-star accolade from the New York Times.
 Our Executive Chef, Philippe Roussel, is among New York's finest, with a career shaped at iconic establishments like Windows on the World and Restaurant Daniel. His unwavering commitment to culinary excellence is evident in every dish, earning praise from the New York Times, Wine Spectator, Eater, Forbes, and more.

 All About the Dough — È tutta questione di impasto
 Located on 8th Avenue in Chelsea, Forno D’Oro delivers immersive dining experiences that celebrate the senses and evoke rich Italian culture. Through architectural design, lavish cocktails, and sophisticated cuisine, we transform everyday meals into unforgettable celebrations.
 Born into a family with a historic pizzeria in Italy, Master Pizzaiolo Salvatore Olivella brings lifelong culinary passion to New York City. Chef Salvatore works seven days a week, tasting every ingredient to ensure absolute perfection for his guests. He honors strict old-world traditions passed down from his father—meaning premium ingredients, flawless execution, and strictly no pineapple on any pizza.

 Our Heritage 
 Where Italy Meets Argentina
 ROMAE is an Italian restaurant and Argentinian steakhouse in New York’s West Village. The name means “of Rome,” a nod to the Italian families who made Argentina home and brought pasta, milanesa, and the table with them. Hand-rolled tortellini sits beside a sizzling Argentine ribeye, and a milanesa napolitana shares the table with Mendoza Malbec, the way it has in Buenos Aires kitchens for generations, now at 57 Seventh Avenue South.
 Tradizione e Passione 
 "Bringing the warm dining legacy of Buenos Aires kitchens straight to Seventh Avenue South."
 Est. 2026 • West Village
 Parrilla Argentina 
 From the Parrilla: Argentinian Steaks Grilled Over Open Flame
 Our parrilla is the beating heart of ROMAE. We fire grass-fed Argentine cuts over an open flame and finish them with house chimichurri, just as they do in Buenos Aires. Come hungry for our 14 oz Argentine Rib Eye, juicy Prime Entraña skirt steak, or smoky Costillas de Asado short ribs. Dining with someone special? The ROMAE West Village Parrillada for two brings skirt steak, NY strip, flap steak, short rib, and picanha to your table on one glorious platter.
 Includes choice of: French Fries, Sweet Potato Fries, or House Salad

 Salmón a la Parrilla 
 From the Italian side of our story, we make our pasta by hand and serve it the way it should be — simple, comforting, and done right. Try our Ricotta Tortellini with braised short ribs in tomato and red wine sauce, pillowy gnocchi, or spinach and ricotta ravioli. And no Italo-Argentine table is complete without a milanesa, order ours a la Napolitana, topped with ham, mozzarella, and tomato sauce, for the dish that perfectly captures both countries on one plate.
 Aperitivo & Entradas 
 Homemade Empanadas & Argentine Starters
 Start the night the Argentine way. Our empanadas are baked fresh and brushed with egg wash, choose from classic beef, chorizo and mozzarella, spicy chicken, and more, or share a half-dozen for the table. Pair them with grilled Provoleta, crispy Calamares Fritos, or the Argentinian Combo of sausage, blood sausage, and sweetbreads, our chef's pick for the full parrilla experience.

 Drinks & Dessert 
 Malbec, Wine & Cocktails to Match
 Great steak deserves great wine. Our list is built around Argentina's signature grape, with Malbec Premium and Malbec Reserva by the glass or bottle, alongside Cabernet, Pinot Noir, Chianti, and crisp whites. Prefer a cocktail? Sip an Aperol Spritz, a refreshing Malbec Verano, or the unmistakably Argentine Fernet and Coke. Save room for a flan con dulce de leche or our Italian Tiramisu to finish.

 Visit ROMAE in the West Village
 You'll find ROMAE at 57 Seventh Avenue South in the heart of New York City's West Village, just steps from the Christopher Street–Sheridan Square station and easy to reach from anywhere in Greenwich Village or Lower Manhattan. Whether it's date night, a celebration, or simply a craving for steak and pasta, our dining room is made for lingering over one more glass of Malbec.

 Our Heritage 
 Where Italy Meets Argentina
 The name ROMAE means "of Rome" — a nod to the millions of Italian families who made Argentina their home over the past century, bringing their pasta, their pizza, and their love of the table with them. That shared heritage is the heart of our kitchen. At ROMAE, hand-rolled tortellini sits comfortably beside a sizzling Argentine ribeye, and a classic milanesa napolitana shares the table with a glass of Mendoza Malbec. This isn't just Italian food or Argentinian food — it's both, the way it's been enjoyed in Buenos Aires kitchens for generations, now right here in the West Village.
 Tradizione e Passione 
 "Bringing the warm dining legacy of Buenos Aires kitchens straight to Seventh Avenue South."

 Located on the corner of West 4th Street and 10th Street, Empellón Taqueria's West Village outpost serves mash up bar snacks and tacos in a casual environment.  The drink menu features margaritas and other cocktails crafted with artisanal Mexican spirits, as well as canned beer and shot specials.

 Empellón Al Pastor (East Village)
 Empellón Al Pastor is a bar located in the East Village on the corner of St. Marks and Avenue A, across the street from Tompkins Square Park. The menu consists of mash up bar snacks and tacos served in a hyper casual environment. Empellón Al Pastor’s drink menu focuses on margaritas, plus 18 beers on tap and a selection of cocktails.

 An instant and enduring success since opening in 2006, this original Boqueria location defined the modern tapas experience in New York City. Inspired by the bustling tapas bars of Barcelona, this vibrant landmark remains a staple for locals and visitors alike. The warm, thoughtfully designed space comes to life at lunch and stays humming through dinner. It’s the neighborhood go-to for Chelsea and Flatiron denizens seeking lively brunches, after-work happy hours, date nights, and group dinners.

 Every neighborhood deserves a great tapas bar. On the Upper East Side, Boqueria delivers. Tucked away on Second Avenue, this Lenox Hill favorite draws a lively crowd for the real-deal Spanish experience. Think sangría-soaked brunches, family-style paellas, and spontaneous tapas sessions at the bar. Whatever the occasion, the room fills with clinking glasses of wine, shared plates, and stories that only get better with each pour.

 Tucked into the cultural heart of D.C., Boqueria Penn Quarter blends bold Catalan flavors with cosmopolitan flair. Just steps from the National Portrait Gallery and Capital One Arena, it's a favorite haunt for power-lunchers, theatergoers, and night owls alike. By day, it’s paella with purpose. By night, the room hums with the clink of sangría glasses and the vibe of a bustling Spanish tapas bar. Slide into a bar seat for one of the city’s most coveted Happy Hours—or gather your crew for the legendary Boqueria brunch.

 In Chicago’s West Loop, Boqueria pulses with the energy of Barcelona and the flavor of the city’s most electric dining district. Locals crowd the lively bar and polished dining room for satisfying lunches and spirited dinners—think succulent jamón, garlicky gambas al ajillo, and classic patatas bravas. Every toast lands sweeter over showstopping sangrías, craft cocktails, and attention-grabbing Spanish wines. Happy Hour draws the after-work crowd, while savvy weekenders book early to claim the city’s most coveted brunch tables.

 Edward's is available for private parties and events at various scales, from large parties to partial and full buyouts. Based on the event and number of people, we will work together to create the desired environment with food and beverage service either from the signature Edward's menu, or using outside catering.
We can accommodate up to 70 guests. If you are planning a private event, reach out to Edward's, and we will set the details in motion.

 About Us 
 Welcome to Bella Luna, your Italian sanctuary on the Upper West Side for 35 years. 
 Located on Columbus Avenue, we're not just a restaurant; we're a neighborhood family. 
 Feast on authentic Italian classics like our irresistible Calamari or signature and new dishes. Don't forget to try our legendary brick-oven pizzas, a piece of Italy right here in NYC. 
 We offer luxury on a budget with recipes that pack a punch of flavor, and a new cocktail menu. 
 Whether it's an intimate dinner or a casual evening, Bella Luna sets the mood for any occasion.

 Chi Restaurant & Bar 
 ———————————————————————— 
 Experience authentic Chinese flavors inspired by all regions of China 
 Conveniently located near Times Square. Our chefs blend traditional recipes with international culinary techniques, creating a menu bursting with flavor and texture. 
 Try our renowned Cucumber Salad infused with Szechuan peppercorn vinaigrette, featured on The Today Show. 
 Savor the creamy richness and peppery kick of our Truffle Beef Tenderloin, a fusion of Chinese stir-frying and French searing. 
 Don't miss our daily limited Braised Pork Belly Pyramid. Enjoy dishes like Lobster with Sticky Rice with perfectly balanced aromatics in our made-in-house XO Sauce. 
 At Chi, cuisine is not limited by region or style, it celebrates culinary collaborations available in New York City's diversity in an intimate dining atmosphere fit for quick bites and long gatherings. 
 The Chefs
​——————— 
 Doctor Tom Lo and Chef Tom Lei opened the kitchen of Chi to New York City's diverse culinary talent as a culinary exchange to collaborate and explore Chinese food. Chi refers to chess in Chinese, and is a tribute to Doctor Lo's son's passion for chess. Doctor Lo and Chef Lei agree that just as pawns play a crucial role in chess, simple ingredients can elevate a dish with proper coordination. The interior design plays music softly for an intimate atmosphere that draws guests' attention to their food and guests, exploring an advanced Chinese menu that is inspired by the culture and flavors of many Chinese regions.

 BIN 141
 Delicious & Healthy Food
 NEW AMERICAN RESTAURANT IN THE EAST VILLAGE 
 "The perfect combination of healthy, organic, vegan, and delicious food 
 in an eclectic atmosphere in the East Village." 
 BIN 141 is the natural evolution of Angelina Cafe, a restaurant that Rafik opened in 2003 in the East Village. Now in 2019, while still keeping the same basic elements and gastronomic philosophy, BIN 141 is the organic transformation that Rafik's restaurant was heading toward: a cozy interior, a welcoming ambience and a much better location (now at the northwest corner of Avenue A and 3rd Street).
 When Rafik decided to open Angelina Cafe, he probably wasn’t expecting to launch a renewed version of his eatery over 15 years later. With the best of both worlds (spacious, windows all around, well located, outdoor seating), he was ready to open his new American restaurant and continue to create his own food under the new banner: BIN 141. NOTE: If you are curious about why the name “BIN 141,” just go to the restaurant and ask Rafik himself.
 Always creative, with the Mediterranean love for grilling and seafood, his training in French cooking and more than 20 years of experience in the USA permeating his food, Rafik decided to focus on always offering healthy and delicious food . And that’s still his main goal: Rafik shops every day for the food he then makes and serves. His creativity and desire to make delicious foods that were more healthy led him, for instance, to coconut milk rather than heavy cream in his bisque soups. He continues to have heart healthy foods and many of which are vegetarian or vegan - and they taste great!
 Bin 141 in a glimpse:
 Healthy, organic, delicious and well priced food.
 Brunch, lunch and fine dining.
 Full bar, draft beer, organic wine and cocktails.
 Happy Hour 5 to 8 PM.
 Take Out and Catering Services available.
 1,000 square feet.
 Capacity for up to 60 people.
 In the East Village (43 Avenue A, NY 10009).
 (646) 822-3628
 It has been over 15 years since Rafik opened Angelina Cafe for the first time, some prime elements are still the same, but some things have changed too. The new restaurant, BIN 141, is a welcoming and friendly venue, which makes it perfect for private as well as corporate events . BIN 141 also has a full bar, with organic cocktails, draft beer and one of the best organic wine selections in the area . And do not forget the impressive and delicious (and vegan) selection of cakes, pastries and gelato .
 Perfect for brunch, lunch and fine dining, or just a late night wine and dessert , BIN 141 still is one of the few places in the East Village where eating is not only a pleasure but also, and always, a unique experience .

 Sarabeth's (Central Park South)
 At Sarabeth's Central Park South, experience the perfect blend of contemporary American cuisine, a welcoming ambiance, and the renowned friendly service that defines our brand. A beloved neighborhood staple and a must-visit destination, Sarabeth's CPS is ideally located near Central Park, just steps from the historic Plaza Hotel, Carnegie Hall, and the Museum of Modern Art (MOMA). Within walking distance of Midtown's top attractions like Columbus Circle, Rockefeller Center, and the Time Warner Center, it's the perfect spot for breakfast, brunch, lunch, or dinner. Indulge in our signature eggs, fluffy pancakes, and famous French toast, or enjoy a delightful weekend brunch with a full bar and handcrafted cocktails.

 Private Dining Venues
 The Skylight Room
 Our semi-private skylight room is the perfect space to host an event. As the name of the room suggests, the beautiful skylight provides the space with natural sunlight which enhances the ambiance of any occasion. With mirrored walls and banquette seating, the room feels spacious, and can comfortably accommodate up to 25 guests.
 Inquire Here 
 The Garden Room
 Our Garden Room is the largest private dining room at Central Park South and can accommodate 30-75 guests for a seated celebration. With its own private bar and restroom, the space is perfect for all event needs.
 Inquire Here 
 The Atrium
 Our most recently renovated space is the glass enclosed Atrium in the center of the restaurant. With a seat right in the center of it all, your guests can take in the sights of the restaurant through the walls, without compromising privacy of your event. With a frosted skylight and lit shutters, the room is a beautiful space for any intimate brunch, or dinner event. This space can accommodate 16 guests comfortably.

 About Us
 IS SARABETH A REAL PERSON? 
 Yes! Sarabeth's is named after Sarabeth Levine who started Sarabeth's a tiny bakery-kitchen in 1981.
 GREAT! DOES SHE STILL RUN ALL THE RESTAURANTS? 
 RBM Restaurant Group now manages the Sarabeth's Restaurants in NYC.
 RIGHT. THEY ALSO MANAGE…. 
 Docks Oyster Bar. It's all part of RBM Restaurant Group.
 YES, THAT'S THEM. SO, WHAT'S SARABETH'S KNOWN FOR? 
 Our Weekend Brunch is quite iconic, from the menu to the quintessential NYC vibe. During the week you can enjoy breakfast and lunch with our lemon ricotta pancakes, grilled cheese alongside hearty salads and delicious muffins. For dinner you must try our crab guacamole and steak frites, oh and don't forget our chicken pot pie and chef's specials. You should really check out the menus here .
 DO YOU BUY LOCAL? 
 Sure.
 ORGANIC? 
 Sometimes.
 WHO IS THE CHEF? 
 Freda Sugarman is our Executive Chef.
 A RESERVATIONS REQUIRED? 
 Reservations are recommended but definitely not required. Just click the link below and reserve up to 30 days in advance. We also hold tables for walk-in guests. Come on by.
 I JUST MIGHT DO THAT. DO THEY TAKE CREDIT CARDS? 
 Absolutely! We accept Visa, MasterCard, America Express, cash and we sell gift cards too.
 HOW DO I GET MY HANDS ON ONE OF THOSE GIFT CARDS? 
 Gift cards to Sarabeth's can be purchased at the restaurant or online via this link right here .
 THIS ALL SOUNDS GREAT, WHAT SHOULD I WEAR? 
 This is New York. Do what you feel, but keep it fresh.
 WHAT IF I NEED A LITTLE PRIVACY? 
 We have multiple private dining options. We offer personalized menus and seamless coordination, tailored to your needs for an unforgettable gathering. Relax and let us handle every detail. You can find out more private dining information here .
 WHAT ABOUT CATERING OFF SITE? 
 You came to the right place. We invite you to enjoy Sarabeth's wherever you want it! We offer customizable catering options designed to suit your needs. Get all the details here .
 DO YOU HAVE ANY PROMOTIONS? 
 Glad you asked. We do offer different promotions at each of our NYC locations from Happy Hour to Live Jazz and days with half priced wine. Be sure to check out our location that most interests you.

 Our menu at Calle Dao Bryant Park blends the bold flavors of Cuban and Chinese cuisine in the heart of Midtown Manhattan, just steps from Bryant Park and minutes from Grand Central Terminal.
 Whether you are searching for dinner near Bryant Park, a lively weekend brunch, weekday lunch, or happy hour before exploring the New York Public Library or catching a Broadway show, our menu offers something for every occasion.
 Signature dishes like Cuban Fried Rice, Mushroom Noodles, handcrafted dumplings, and refreshing mojitos make Calle Dao a top choice for dining near Bryant Park.

 About Calle Dao Bryant Park – Cuban Chinese Fusion Restaurant in Midtown Manhattan
 Located just steps from Bryant Park in the heart of Midtown Manhattan, Calle Dao Bryant Park is a vibrant Cuban Chinese fusion restaurant offering lunch, brunch, dinner, happy hour, and private dining in New York City. Our restaurant near Grand Central Terminal has become a favorite gathering place for locals, commuters, and visitors looking for bold flavors, handcrafted cocktails, and a lively dining atmosphere near one of Manhattan's most iconic parks.
 The Bryant Park neighborhood is often called Midtown Manhattan's town square, known for its seasonal gardens, open-air events, and classic New York charm. Whether you are meeting colleagues for lunch near Bryant Park, enjoying happy hour after work, or gathering with friends for dinner in Midtown Manhattan, Calle Dao offers a welcoming space to relax, celebrate, and enjoy unforgettable cuisine.
 Our convenient Midtown location near Grand Central Station also makes Calle Dao a popular meeting spot for group dinners, celebrations, and private events. From birthday gatherings and corporate dinners to graduation celebrations for nearby colleges such as Guttman Community College, ASA College, and Berkeley College, our team helps guests create memorable moments in the heart of New York City.
 Calle Dao is inspired by Havana's once thriving El Barrio Chino, or Chinatown, which was once the largest Chinese community in Latin America. In the late 1800s, Chinese immigrants arrived in Cuba and began blending their culinary traditions with the bold ingredients and flavors of Cuban cooking. The result was a unique fusion cuisine that combined the warmth of Cuban hospitality with the techniques and flavors of Chinese kitchens.
 At Calle Dao, our menu celebrates this vibrant culinary heritage. Signature dishes blend Cuban staples with Asian flavors, creating a menu that is both comforting and exciting. Our handcrafted cocktail program, created by mixologist Joy Daniel, reflects the same fusion spirit by combining historical inspiration with modern ingredients. The Calle Dao Mojito pairs rum and ginger liqueur with shiso leaves, lemongrass, fresh lime juice and a Champagne top, and the Opium mixes bourbon with tamarind, ruby red grapefruit, lemon and poppy seeds.
 The restaurant's design, created by owner Marco Britti, evokes the warmth and character of old Havana with whitewashed walls, distressed wood, whirring ceiling fans, and vibrant accents inspired by Chinese artwork and spices. The space brings together two cultures and creates a setting that feels both energetic and welcoming.
 Today, Calle Dao Bryant Park continues that tradition by offering a unique dining experience where Cuban and Chinese culinary influences meet in the heart of Midtown Manhattan. Just moments from Bryant Park and Grand Central Terminal, our restaurant invites guests to step into a lively atmosphere, enjoy bold flavors, and experience a modern interpretation of a historic culinary story.
Calle Dao Bryant Park is located in Midtown Manhattan at 38 West 39th Street, just steps from Bryant Park and a short walk from Grand Central Terminal, the New York Public Library, and the Theater District.

 About Us 
 Midori Sushi & Steakhouse 
 Welcome to Midori Sushi and Steakhouse, an exquisite culinary destination nestled in the heart of Long Island, where the art of Japanese cuisine and the sizzle of expertly grilled steaks converge to create an unforgettable dining experience.
 At Midori, we pride ourselves on offering a unique fusion of traditional Japanese flavors and innovative culinary techniques. Our chefs, masters of their craft, skillfully blend the freshest, highest-quality ingredients to craft a menu that caters to the discerning palate of our guests. Whether you're a sushi aficionado, a lover of sizzling hibachi, or simply seeking an elevated dining experience, Midori has something to tantalize your taste buds.
 Step into our sleek and modern ambiance, where the warm glow of ambient lighting sets the stage for an evening of culinary delight. Our commitment to creating a welcoming atmosphere extends beyond our kitchen, as our attentive and friendly staff is dedicated to ensuring your every need is met.
 Indulge in the artistry of our sushi bar, where our talented sushi chefs transform the finest cuts of fish into edible masterpieces. From classic rolls to innovative creations, each bite is a testament to our dedication to culinary excellence.
 For those seeking an interactive dining adventure, our hibachi tables offer a front-row seat to the excitement of teppanyaki-style cooking. Watch as our skilled chefs showcase their culinary prowess, expertly grilling premium steaks, fresh seafood, and market-fresh vegetables with flair and precision.
 Midori is not just a restaurant; it's a celebration of flavors, a gathering place for friends and family, and a destination for those who appreciate the art of fine dining. Join us for an unparalleled gastronomic journey where each dish is a work of art, and every moment is an opportunity to savor the extraordinary.
 Whether you're a local resident or a visitor to Long Island, Midori Sushi and Steakhouse invites you to experience the pinnacle of Japanese cuisine in a setting that exudes warmth, sophistication, and culinary passion. Come, immerse yourself in the symphony of flavors that is Midori.

 About
 Dylan Murphy's is an established Irish pub located in the heart of the upper eastside. Its many regulars love it for its top notch pub food, amazing jukebox, variety of sports programming, and friendly staff. Dylan Murphy's has hosted people from all corners of the world who come here for the jovial atmosphere, excellent service and quality conversations with the staff and locals. The pub is located just steps from the Q, 4, 5 and 6 trains near the corner of East 82nd Street and Third Avenue at 1453 Third Avenue, New York, NY 10028.

 VIEW MENU 
 Experience fine American Cuisine with a Southern Italian influence.
 Enjoy boutique wines, craft beer and classic cocktails in a unique atmosphere and spacious garden. 
 In summer, the carefully tended garden is magical, and in winter, the exquisitely decorated restaurant is cozy and intimate. This place is perfect for a gathering of good friends, or a romantic date. Oh! And the food! The food is heaven. If I could eat their Creamy Polenta with Poached eggs every day, I would be a happy chick! Their menu changes relatively often, and I have always found something I love. This place is a piece of heaven in Brooklyn!
 Danielle D. 
 There's a lot of choice in Brooklyn and this place stands out. It's got character, quality and choice on so many levels. There are 4 seating spaces now that the garden is open and the chef seems to be continually exploring new flavor combinations. I'm not a wine connoisseur but wines are not like anything I've had before. Did I mention the ambiance?
 Yankanuk 
 I stayed nearby at the Box House Hotel. The staff recommended Milk & Roses for breakfast. Went there with a friend who is Italian. We walked in to captivating, intimate setting. We could have been in Europe. Asked to be seated in the garden in the back. The setting was rustic/adorable. She said the bkft menu was as if she was back in Italy. Our server was Italian too. Food was excellent!! Espresso was delicious! Absolutely plan to go back. Highly recommend.
 Elizabeth H

 Artesano
 Welcome to Artesano, NYC
 Our Concept
 The concept was created with the various talents of the founding business partners in mind. Each individual brought a certain “artisan” quality to cultivate the unique latin experience that has become ARTESANO today. 
 Our Name
 The name Artesano came to be, as we looked around at our team and saw a group of Artisans excelling in their various crafts. We knew that every aspect of our restaurant concept needed to be executed in an elegant and deliberate way, from the corn husk installation above our bar, to our stone plates handmade and imported from Peru.
 SOME OF THE BEST SENSORY EXPERIENCES HAPPEN ON A PERUVIAN PLATE
 In just one bite, you are able to taste the sentiments and nostalgia from a fusion of continents. Peruvian gastronomy holds something that other cuisines lack, in that its influence and inclusiveness has opened the door for the marriages of many cultures and thus have ingrained themselves into the traditional gastronomic experience.
 Above all else, we pride ourselves on the notion that this kitchen is not static. Peru has been chosen as the best culinary destination of the world for over a decade and this is no coincidence, as its locals have never been afraid of pushing the limits and experimenting in the kitchen.
 'This is a delicate dance they have mastered, because of their respect for the process, product, seasons and ecosystems that the country has to offer.'
 'So long as the world continues to evolve, so will the kitchen. The end of possibilities is nowhere in sight.'
 Rodrigo Fernandini
